sources.title: Foundation Engineering Analysis and Design - geotechnical characterization, SPT, groundwater, consolidation, and compaction boundaries
safe_claims: Subsurface exploration provides ground stratigraphy, soil and rock properties, groundwater conditions, geotechnical parameters, settlement inputs, and construction-problem warnings for foundation design.
Foundation design must check both safety/stability and performance/serviceability; settlement can govern even when stability is adequate.
Soil properties depend on density, void ratio, water content, effective stress, drainage condition, compressibility, strength, and permeability.
Groundwater level affects bearing capacity and settlement and should be observed during exploration.
SPT gives an N value from the last 300 mm of split-spoon penetration and provides disturbed soil samples for basic physical property tests.
Saturated clay consolidation is time-dependent as excess pore pressure dissipates; secondary consolidation continues after primary consolidation.
The captured Standard Proctor detail is limited to the source example of MSE backfill placement and compaction.

sources.title: Building Structures Illustrated - foundation system context
safe_claims: A foundation supports and anchors the superstructure and transmits loads safely into the earth.
Foundation selection responds to soil, rock, and water conditions below the building.
Shallow foundations fit stable near-surface soil with adequate bearing capacity.
Mat foundations distribute concentrated loads and help manage differential settlement.
Pile or caisson foundations are used when building loads exceed supporting-soil bearing capacity.
